events.title: Galileo Is Warned Against Teaching Heliocentrism
events.description: The Catholic Church formally ordered Galileo Galilei to stop teaching or defending the idea that the Earth moves around the Sun. The order came as church authorities moved against the Copernican view of the cosmos.
events.significance: The ruling set up a decades-long clash between scientific inquiry and church authority. That clash ended in Galileo's trial in 1633.

events.title: Napoleon Escapes from Elba
events.description: Napoleon Bonaparte slipped away from his exile on the Mediterranean island of Elba. He sailed for France with about 1,200 men.
events.significance: His escape began the Hundred Days, a final bid to regain power. It ended at Waterloo.

events.title: Grand Canyon Becomes a National Park
events.description: President Woodrow Wilson signed legislation that made the Grand Canyon a national park. The law protected most of the vast gorge carved by the Colorado River in Arizona.
events.significance: The designation safeguarded one of the world's best-known natural landmarks. Today it draws millions of visitors each year.

events.title: The February 26 Incident in Tokyo
events.description: Young nationalist officers of the Imperial Japanese Army led troops into central Tokyo in an attempted coup. They assassinated several political leaders.
events.significance: The coup failed, but it left the military with far more influence over Japan's government in the years before World War II.

events.title: World Trade Center Bombing
events.description: A car bomb exploded in the underground parking garage beneath the World Trade Center in New York City. Six people were killed and more than 1,000 were injured.
events.significance: It was one of the first major Islamist terror attacks on U.S. soil. It also foreshadowed the attacks on the same complex in 2001.
